blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Reading demand and supply signals is what turns a planner into a good one. The numbers by themselves are flat. The planner's job is to listen for the signals underneath them: a small shift in reorder patterns, a quiet drop in fill rate, a supplier suddenly asking for longer lead times, a distributor pushing harder for promotions.

Each of these tells you something. The reorder pattern suggests demand is starting to move. The fill rate drop tells us supply is tightening. The supplier asking for longer times is signalling trouble upstream. The distributor pushing for promotions may be sitting on too much stock.

Planners who learn to read these signals early are usually two or three weeks ahead of the problem — which, in supply chain, is the difference between a quick fix and a crisis.

items.q: According to the text, what are the numbers like on their own?
items.why: "The numbers by themselves are flat." — sozinhos não carregam contexto.

items.q: What does a quiet drop in fill rate tell us?
items.why: "The fill rate drop tells us supply is tightening."

items.q: A distributor pushing harder for promotions may suggest that…
options: the distributor is sitting on too much stock
the distributor has run out of stock
demand is about to fall to zero
items.why: Inferência: "The distributor pushing for promotions may be sitting on too much stock." — quer empurrar o excesso.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A supplier asking for longer lead times should simply be ignored.
Catching a signal early can turn a crisis into a quick fix.
Two small signals together can matter.
A single number, read alone, rarely tells the whole story.
items.why: Inferência: o texto trata cada sinal como algo a ser lido, não ignorado.

items.q: The phrase "two or three weeks ahead of the problem" suggests that reading signals early gives a planner…
options: time to act before the crisis hits
a way to avoid talking to suppliers
a guarantee that shortages never happen
items.why: Inferência: estar à frente do problema é justamente ter tempo de agir — a diferença entre conserto rápido e crise.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie orientando uma planejadora júnior. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So let's talk about last month, because I think you could have caught that shortage a good three weeks earlier. I'm not saying this to be hard on you — I'm saying it because the signals were there.

There were two of them, and neither was dramatic. First, the reorder pattern from the northern accounts shifted. Nothing huge — a few days earlier than usual, a slightly bigger quantity. On its own, easy to miss. Second, our main supplier quietly asked for two extra days of lead time. Again, small. But put those two together and the story changes: demand was creeping up while supply was getting slower.

That's the whole point I want you to take away. One small signal is noise. Two small signals pointing the same way is a message. When demand moves up and supply tightens at the same time, you don't wait for the fill rate to fall — you act.

So here's my rule, and I want you to make it a habit: read the data every single morning, not just when something is already on fire. The best planners see the problem three weeks before anyone else does.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How much earlier does Sophie say the junior planner could have caught the shortage?
items.why: "you could have caught that shortage a good three weeks earlier."

items.q: What were the two signals the planner missed?
options: A shift in the reorder pattern and a supplier asking for more lead time
A budget cut and a staff shortage
A price rise and a new competitor
A drop in fill rate and a distributor promotion
items.why: "the reorder pattern… shifted" e "our main supplier quietly asked for two extra days of lead time."

items.q: Why does Sophie say the two signals together mattered more than each alone?
options: Because they cancelled each other out
Because demand was rising while supply was slowing at the same time
Because they came from the same account
items.why: "demand was creeping up while supply was getting slower" — os dois na mesma direção viram uma mensagem.

items.q: When Sophie says "One small signal is noise. Two small signals pointing the same way is a message," she is suggesting that…
options: context and combination turn weak data into meaning
planners should ignore all small signals
noise and messages are the same thing
only large signals are worth acting on
items.why: Inferência: sinais isolados são ruído; combinados e na mesma direção, viram informação acionável.

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's tone toward the junior planner?
options: Corrective but supportive, teaching a habit
items.why: Inferência: ela diz que não é para ser dura, e termina propondo uma rotina concreta — corrige, mas ensina.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The reorder pattern showed a small shift toward earlier orders." A shift here is…
items.why: Shift = mudança, deslocamento no padrão.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When supply starts to ___, fill rates fall and shortages follow."
items.why: To tighten = apertar; a oferta aperta e o abastecimento fica escasso.

items.q: "A supplier asking for longer lead times often signals trouble upstream." Upstream refers to…
options: the earlier stages of the supply chain, toward the source
items.why: Upstream = a montante, mais perto da origem/fornecimento.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The ___ was sitting on too much stock, so it pushed harder for promotions."
items.why: Distributor = distribuidor, quem tinha excesso de estoque para escoar.

items.q: "A reorder is triggered when stock drops below the set point." A reorder is…
options: a request to cancel an order
a change to the delivery address
a refund on a returned item
a new order to replenish stock
items.why: Reorder = pedido de reposição, para repor o estoque.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de planejamento e supply chain. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We were sitting on three months of excess stock." To sit on something means to…
options: hold it without using or moving it
items.why: Sit on = ficar segurando algo parado, sem escoar.

items.q: "Sophie told the team to keep an eye on the northern accounts." This means to…
items.why: Keep an eye on = monitorar de perto, ficar de olho.

items.q: "Two small signals together can flag up a problem early." To flag up means to…
items.why: Flag up = sinalizar, chamar a atenção para algo.

items.q: "If we catch the signal early, we can get ahead of the shortage." To get ahead of something means to…
items.why: Get ahead of = antecipar-se, agir antes que o problema estoure.

items.q: "Reading the data every morning helps you stay on top of the numbers." To stay on top of means to…
options: remain fully in control and up to date
items.why: Stay on top of = manter-se no controle e atualizado sobre algo.
